Information related to hardware dimension.
Class that describes an instance of Hardware.
A Package that contains AI software or an AI model.

Identifies the full text of a LicenseAddition.
Temporary endeavor with a beginning and an end and that must be used to create a unique product, service or result.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: trackStar
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: ("Track\*" in the SSVC spec) The vulnerability contains specific characteristics that may require closer monitoring for changes. CISA recommends remediating Track\* vulnerabilities within standard update timelines.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: review
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Used when someone reviews the Element.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: qualityAssessmentReport
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A reference to a quality assessment for a package.
Test Process defines the testing process for an element.
Provides information about the primary purpose of an Element.
Provides an IntegrityMethod with which the integrity of an Element can be asserted.
Authentication protocol used by a server.
Abstract class for additional text intended to be added to a License, but which is not itself a standalone License.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: directory
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The file represents a directory and all content stored in that directory.
Expression for the export control classification.
Information about different steps of the training process.
Prescribes the storage of a product.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: componentNotPresent
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The software is not affected because the vulnerable component is not in the product.
RequirementVerification class defines the base properties of a verification.
A reference to a resource outside the scope of SPDX 3 content related to an Element.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: specification
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A specification is a detailed document (or set of documents) that describes the requirements, design, behavior, or other characteristics of a system, component, or process so that all stakeholders have a clear, unambiguous reference.
Metric used to evaluate the AI model.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: module
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The Element is a module of a piece of software.
A specification is a detailed description of the design, requirements, or features of a product, process, or system.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: runtimeAnalysisReport
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A reference to a runtime analysis report for a package.
A type of extension consisting of a list of name value pairs.
This class represents the process involved in manufacturing products.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: descendantOf
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The `from` Element is a descendant of each `to` Element.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: blake2b256
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: BLAKE2b algorithm with a digest size of 256, as defined in [RFC 7693](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/rfc7693/) Section 4.
Additional relevance information.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: support
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The artifact has been released, and is supported from the supplier. There is a validUntilDate that can provide additional information about the duration of support.
Class that describes an instance of VirtualHardware.
A distinct article or unit related to Software.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: securityOther
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A reference to related security information of unspecified type.
Identifies all the text and metadata associated with a license in the license XML format.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: staticAnalysisReport
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A reference to a static analysis report for a package.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: other
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The Element doesn't fit into any of the other categories.
The location for picking up a package or item.
Class that describes a process.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: contains
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The `from` Element contains each `to` Element.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: hasDeclaredLicense
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The `from` Artifact was discovered to actually contain each `to` AnyLicenseInfo (for example, as detected by automated tooling).

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: hasTest
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Every `to` Element is a test artifact for the `from` Element (`from` hasTest `to`), during a LifecycleScopeType period.
Contains a URL where the License or LicenseAddition can be found in use.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: review
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A examination or checking of documentation, records, processes, or systems to confirm compliance or adherence with an upper level requirement. Typically done as peer review, offline review or review meeting.
evidenceCategory refers to a category of documented or observable proof.
Describes a relationship between one or more elements.
ResponsibilityChangeAction refers to the transfer of responsibility from one party to another.
Describes a certain part of a file.
A Package that contains a dataset.
Specifies the time an artifact was built.
A buildId is a locally unique identifier used by a builder to identify a unique instance of a build produced by it.
Base domain class from which all other SPDX 3 domain classes derive.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: platform
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The Element represents a runtime environment.
Links a vulnerability and one or more elements designating the latter as products not affected by the vulnerability.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: invokedBy
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The `from` Element was invoked by the `to` Agent, during a LifecycleScopeType period (for example, a Build element that describes a build step).
An Organization representing the SPDX Project.
Identifies when the Element was originally created.
A license exception that is listed on the SPDX Exceptions list.
Records any relevant background information or additional comments about the origin of the package.
A canonical, unique, immutable identifier.
City is a specific name used to define a locality.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: hasMetadata
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Every `to` Element is metadata about the `from` Element (`from` hasMetadata `to`).
A characterization of some aspect of an Element that is associated with the Element in a generalized fashion.
Refers to any object that stores content on a computer.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: cve
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures identifiers, an identifier for a specific software flaw defined within the official CVE Dictionary and that conforms to the [CVE specification](https://csrc.nist.gov/glossary/term/cve_id).
ManufactureAction represents the act of creating a product by a manufacturing process.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: medium
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The third-highest level of risk posed by an AI system.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: bower
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A reference to a Bower package. The package locator format, looks like `package#version`, is defined in the "install" section of [Bower API documentation](https://bower.io/docs/api/#install).

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: track
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The vulnerability does not require action at this time. The organization would continue to track the vulnerability and reassess it if new information becomes available. CISA recommends remediating Track vulnerabilities within standard update timelines.

Provide the enumeration of possible decisions in the [Stakeholder-Specific Vulnerability Categorization (SSVC) decision tree](https://www.cisa.gov/stakeholder-specific-vulnerability-categorization-ssvc).

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: hasAssociatedVulnerability
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Used to associate a `from` Artifact with each `to` Vulnerability.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: high
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: When a CVSS score is between 7.0 - 8.9.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: serious
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The highest level of risk posed by an AI system.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: log
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Time-stamped records capturing system or operational data recorded as usually as a response to specific triggers in a specified environment.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: validatedOn
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The `from` Element has been validated on the `to` Element(s).

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: follows
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The `to` Element succeeds the `from` Element, establishing a unidirectional sequence. This succession is defined as chronological, procedural, or logical. It is used to represent either a temporal order (e.g., in a workflow) or a logical order for processing and traversal (e.g., in an ordered list).

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: hardware
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The element follows the Hardware profile specification.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: yes
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Indicates presence of the field.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: blake2b512
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: BLAKE2b algorithm with a digest size of 512, as defined in [RFC 7693](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/rfc7693/) Section 4.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: no
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Indicates absence of the field.
Street address includes a street number, name and unit ID to identify a specific street.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: ocsp
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Online Certificate Status Protocol, or OCSP, is a common scheme used to maintain the security of a server and other network resources.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: swhid
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: SoftWare Hash IDentifier, a persistent intrinsic identifier for digital artifacts, such as files, trees (also known as directories or folders), commits, and other objects typically found in version control systems. The format of the identifiers is defined in the [SWHID specification](https://www.swhid.org/swhid-specification/v1.2/) ([ISO/IEC 18670](https://www.iso.org/standard/89985.html)). They typically look like `swh:1:cnt:94a9ed024d3859793618152ea559a168bbcbb5e2`.
The destruction process is defined in this process.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: orcidid
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: [Open Researcher and Contributor ID (ORCID) iD](https://info.orcid.org/what-is-orcid/) is a unique identifier for authors and contributors in scholarly communication; as a subset of the International Standard Name Identifier (ISNI), it typically appears as a URI such as `https://orcid.org/0000-0002-1825-0097`.
A license addition that is not listed on the SPDX Exceptions List.

rdf:Description.sh:message: https://spdx.org/rdf/3.1/terms/SupplyChain/ModifyProcess is an abstract class and should not be instantiated directly. Instantiate a subclass instead.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: source
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: SBOM created directly from the development environment, source files, and included dependencies used to build a product artifact.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: tracedToDetail
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: the `from` Requirement is refined and further elaborated by each `to` Requirement, which contains more detailed implementation information.
This individual element was defined by the spec.
Type of data in a dataset.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: riskAssessment
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A reference to a risk assessment for a package.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: other
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Every `to` Element is related to the `from` Element where the relationship type is not described by any of the SPDX relationship types (this relationship is directionless).

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: observation
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Documentation of direct monitoring or witnessing of the demonstration of processes, tests, or any kind of system responses during a specified timeframe under specified environmental conditions.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: swhid
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: SoftWare Hash IDentifier, a persistent intrinsic identifier for digital artifacts, such as files, trees (also known as directories or folders), commits, and other objects typically found in version control systems. The format of the identifiers is defined in the [SWHID specification](https://www.swhid.org/swhid-specification/v1.2/) ([ISO/IEC 18670](https://www.iso.org/standard/89985.html)). They typically look like `swh:1:cnt:94a9ed024d3859793618152ea559a168bbcbb5e2`.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: deployed
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: In addition to being supported by the supplier, the software is known to have been deployed and is in use. For a software as a service provider, this implies the software is now available as a service.
A map of Element identifiers that are used within an SpdxDocument but defined external to that SpdxDocument.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: other
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Any other specialized or custom verification method that fits the context.
The relative file name of a file to be excluded from the `PackageVerificationCode`.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: other
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: An authentication protocol not covered by one of the other AuthenticationProtocolTypes.
An Individual Value for Element representing a set of Elements with cardinality (number/count) of zero.

**DEPRECATED in SPDX 3.1.** Use [/Software/artifactSize](../../Software/Properties/artifactSize.md) instead.
Size of the dataset.
Assessment of an Element for export control classification.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: image
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Data is a collection of images such as pictures of animals.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: packagedBy
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Every `to` Element is a packaged instance of the `from` Element (`from` packagedBy `to`).
The measure of mass refers to the quantity of matter in an object or substance.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: other
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A generic contact point to be used when the contact type does not match any of the other options.
The CreateProcess refers to the abstract process class that can be used to represent the process of creation of a product.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: providesSupportFor
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The `from` Agent provides support for each `to` Artifact. The use of the `providesSupportFor` type is constrained to `SupportRelationship` classed relationships.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: rorid
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: [Research Organization Registry (ROR) identifier](https://ror.org/about/) is a unique identifier for research and funding organization, typically expressed in its preferred URI form such as `https://ror.org/02mhbdp94`.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: other
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Used when the type does not match any of the other options.
This individual element was defined by the spec.
A license that is not listed on the SPDX License List.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: support
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A contact point for support.
Unit in which energy is measured.
Describes if any sensitive personal information is present in the dataset.
Identifies the name of an Element as designated by the creator.
Identifies the full text of a LicenseAddition, in SPDX templating format.
Enumeration of verification types.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: noAssertion
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Data type is not known.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: lexid
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: LEX Identifier is a Uniform Resource Name (URN) for sources of law within the [LEX namespace](https://www.iana.org/assignments/urn-formal/lex), as defined in [RFC 9676](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/rfc9676/) (e.g., `urn:lex:it:stato:decreto.legislativo:2018-08-10;101`).
Portion of an AnyLicenseInfo representing a set of licensing information where all elements apply.
Products out of specification require a resolution action. This is the action of resolution.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: notAutomated
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Level 0 - Not automated. No automation. The operator fully controls the system.
This is the state of an affected Element at a specific moment in time.
Provides an EPSS assessment for a vulnerability.
Abstract ancestor class for all vulnerability assessments.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: assumes
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The `from` Element assumes each `to` Assumption.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: filesystemImage
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The Element is a file system image that can be written to a disk (or virtual) partition.
Portion of an AnyLicenseInfo representing a set of licensing information where only one of the elements applies.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: inlineMitigationsAlreadyExist
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Built-in inline controls or mitigations prevent an adversary from leveraging the vulnerability.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: productMetadata
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A reference to additional product metadata such as reference within organization's product catalog.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: hasVariant
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Every `to` Element is a variant the `from` Element (`from` hasVariant `to`).
Abstract class representing a License or an OrLaterOperator.
A physical location is a tangible, geographically identifiable place where objects, people, or assets exist or operate.
A distinct unit representing a constraint associated with an item's use in a system.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: requirement
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The Element provides a requirement needed as input for another Element.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: inconclusive
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Inconclusive refers to a result or outcome from a verification, test, or analysis that cannot be clearly classified as either positive (successful, pass) or negative (failed, reject). An inconclusive result means there was not enough clear evidence, data, or signal to make a definitive determination, and further investigation or additional testing is necessary. An inconclusive result always shall need a comment on it.
An assertion made in relation to one or more elements.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: clickthrough
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Dataset is not publicly available and can only be accessed after affirmatively accepting terms on a clickthrough webpage.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: hasProvidedDependency
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The `from` Element has a dependency on each `to` Element, dependency is not in the distributed artifact, but assumed to be provided, during a LifecycleScopeType period.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: functionalSafety
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The element follows the FunctionalSafety profile specification.
Threshold that was used for computation of a metric described in the metric field.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: exportControlAssessment
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A reference to an export control assessment for a package.
The record of destruction is entered in this action.
This property is used to denote the root Element(s) of a tree of elements contained in a BOM.
A verificationUID is a unique identifier assigned to a Verification item.
The measure of length refers to the dimension of an object or space that describes how long it is, typically expressed in various units depending on the system of measurement being used.
Defines the beginning of a range.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: ibid
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: [International Business Identifier (IBID)](https://ekys.org/business_identifiers/) is a verifiable unique identifier for legal entities as defined in the [ISO/DIS 25500-3](https://www.iso.org/standard/87705.html) draft standard. It is composed of three data elements: the International Business Registration Number (IBRN), the legal name, and the date of origin formatted as eight numeric characters (YYYYMMDD). Each element is separated by a pipe character (`|`) (e.g., `US-DE.BER:3031657|Code Management Association|19990420`).
Provides the result of an export control assessment.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: operations
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The element follows the Operations profile specification.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: pretrainedOn
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The `from` Element has been pretrained on the `to` Element(s).
The class that helps note down the quantity of energy consumption and the unit used for measurement.
A collection of SPDX Elements that could potentially be serialized.
A transport route refers to the specific path or network used to move people, goods, data, or resources from one location to another.
Location of a specific action.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: firmware
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The Element provides low level control over a device's hardware.
Provides a CVSS version 3 assessment for a vulnerability.
Specifies the type of an annotation.

rdf:Description.sh:message: https://spdx.org/rdf/3.1/terms/ExpandedLicensing/ExtendableLicense is an abstract class and should not be instantiated directly. Instantiate a subclass instead.

rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Identifies the text of one or more copyright notices for a software Package, File or Snippet, if any.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: container
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The Element is a container image which can be used by a container runtime application.
Information related to physical hardware.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: attend
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The vulnerability requires attention from the organization's internal, supervisory-level individuals. Necessary actions include requesting assistance or information about the vulnerability, and may involve publishing a notification either internally and/or externally. CISA recommends remediating Attend vulnerabilities sooner than standard update timelines.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: iscc
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: [International Standard Content Code (ISCC)](https://iscc.io/) is a content-derived identifier standardized by [ISO 24138](https://www.iso.org/standard/77899.html) for identifying digital assets. ISCC can be used in conjunction with other schemes, such as DOI, ISAN, ISBN, ISRC, ISSN and ISWC. A standard ISCC-CODE is build from multiple ISCC-UNITs. Each unit serve a different purpose. An ISCC-CODE typically look like `ISCC:KACT4EBWK27737D2AYCJRAL5Z36G76RFRMO4554RU26HZ4ORJGIVHDI`.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: specification
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The Element is a plan, guideline or strategy how to create, perform or analyze an application.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: copiedTo
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The `from` Element has been copied to each `to` Element.

rdf:Description.sh:message: https://spdx.org/rdf/3.1/terms/SupplyChain/ModifyAction is an abstract class and should not be instantiated directly. Instantiate a subclass instead.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: hasTestCase
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Every `to` Element is a test case for the `from` Element (`from` hasTestCase `to`).

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: iswc
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: [International Standard Musical Work Code (ISWC)](https://www.iswc.org/iswc) is an 11-character unique identifier standardized by [ISO 15707](https://www.iso.org/standard/83125.html) for musical works (compositions) as distinct from specific recordings. While the "ISWC" label and grouping separators (dots and hyphens) are used for human readability, they shall be omitted when the identifier is stored electronically (e.g., `T0017812031`).
Connects a vulnerability and an element designating the element as a product affected by the vulnerability.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: binaryArtifact
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A reference to binary artifacts related to a package.
Specification basis for the export control classification.
The AssemblyProcess represents the process of creating a product by assembling a set of components, potentially in a way that allows for at disassembly (at least partially).
A key with an Element.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: other
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Any specification that does not fall under any of the other entries.
Describes how an Agent provides support for an Artifact.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: documentation
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The Element is documentation.
Information related to hardware dimension.
Sponsor of the project.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: dependsOn
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The `from` Element depends on each `to` Element, during a LifecycleScopeType period.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: configures
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The `from` Element is a configuration applied to each `to` Element, during a LifecycleScopeType period.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: sha3_384
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: SHA-3 with a digest length of 384, as defined in [FIPS 202](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/fips/202/final).
A state is an instance that describes what a system, component, subsystem, process, or project has achieved at any given time.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: hasAddedFile
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Every `to` Element is a file added to the `from` Element (`from` hasAddedFile `to`).
Software provided as a service over a network.
A collection of Elements, not necessarily with unifying context.
A class for describing the energy consumption incurred by an AI model in different stages of its lifecycle.
QUDT unit is used for measurement criteria based on product type, region and use.
Dimensions generally refer to measurable extents or attributes that define the size, shape, or scale of an object, system, or concept.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: altDownloadLocation
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A reference to an alternative download location.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: urlScheme
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: [Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) Schemes](https://www.iana.org/assignments/uri-schemes/uri-schemes.xhtml). The scheme used in order to locate a resource.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: categorical
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Data that is classified into a discrete number of categories, such as the eye color of a population of people.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: other
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Any other units of energy measurement.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: sha3_512
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: SHA-3 with a digest length of 512, as defined in [FIPS 202](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/fips/202/final).
Provides an ExternalMap of Element identifiers.
Version identifier for the item.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: analyzed
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: SBOM generated through analysis of artifacts (e.g., executables, packages, containers, and virtual machine images) after its build. Such analysis generally requires a variety of heuristics. In some contexts, this may also be referred to as a "3rd party" SBOM.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: issueTracker
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A reference to the issue tracker for a package.
A concrete subclass of Element used by Individuals in the Core profile.
A contact point from an Artifact to an Agent.
Information related to massOfHardware physical hardware.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: directDownload
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Dataset is publicly available and can be downloaded directly.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: conformsTo
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The `from` Element conforms to each `to` Assumption or Specification.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: webpage
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Absolute URL that can be used to locate a resource, as defined in [RFC 7230](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/rfc7230/) Section 2.7.1 or Section 2.7.2.
A string in the license expression format.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: md5
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: MD5 message-digest algorithm, as defined in [RFC 1321](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/rfc1321/).

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: evidence
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The Element is the evidence that a specification or requirement has been fulfilled.

Type of support that is associated with an artifact.
Provides a map of a property name to a value.
Identifies who or what supplied the artifact or VulnAssessmentRelationship referenced by the Element.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: bic
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Business Identifier Code (BIC), also known as SWIFT-BIC or SWIFT code, is a unique 8 or 11-character alphanumeric code standardized by [ISO 9362](https://www.iso.org/standard/84108.html) to identify financial and non-financial institutions (e.g., `BBWCUS33`).
Provides a place for the SPDX data creator to record the package URL string (in accordance with the Package URL specification) for a software Package.
Provides an unambiguous mechanism for conveying a URI fragment portion of an Element ID.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: endOfSupport
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: There is a defined end of support for the artifact from the supplier. This may also be referred to as end of life. There is a validUntilDate that can be used to signal when support ends for the artifact.
An Individual Value for License when no assertion can be made about its actual value.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: delegatedTo
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The `from` Agent is delegating an action to the Agent of the `to` Relationship (which shall be of type invokedBy), during a LifecycleScopeType (e.g. the `to` invokedBy Relationship is being done on behalf of `from`).
This is the planned product associated with the change of responsibility.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: noSupport
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: There is no support for the artifact from the supplier, consumer assumes any support obligations.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: runtime
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relationship has specific context implications during the execution phase of an element.

A gitoid of type blob is a unique hash of a binary artifact. A gitoid may represent either an [Artifact Identifier](https://github.com/omnibor/spec/blob/eb1ee5c961c16215eb8709b2975d193a2007a35d/spec/SPEC.md#artifact-identifier-types) for the software artifact or an [Input Manifest Identifier](https://github.com/omnibor/spec/blob/eb1ee5c961c16215eb8709b2975d193a2007a35d/spec/SPEC.md#input-manifest-identifier) for the software artifact's associated [Artifact Input Manifest](https://github.com/omnibor/spec/blob/eb1ee5c961c16215eb8709b2975d193a2007a35d/spec/SPEC.md#artifact-input-manifest); this ambiguity exists because the Artifact Input Manifest is itself an artifact, and the gitoid of that artifact is its valid identifier. Gitoids calculated on software artifacts (Snippet, File, or Package Elements) should be recorded in the SPDX 3 SoftwareArtifact's contentIdentifier property. Gitoids calculated on the Artifact Input Manifest (Input Manifest Identifier) should be recorded in the SPDX 3 Element's externalIdentifier property. See [OmniBOR Specification](https://github.com/omnibor/spec/), a minimalistic specification for describing software [Artifact Dependency Graphs](https://github.com/omnibor/spec/blob/eb1ee5c961c16215eb8709b2975d193a2007a35d/spec/SPEC.md#artifact-dependency-graph-adg).
